prompt:
On-call wants response times per service. Add a command that computes them. It runs as `python -m logsift.latency OUTPUT_CSV FILE [FILE ...]`.

Read the FILE arguments the same way the summary report reads them, so lines that do not parse are skipped and reported as usual. An entry has a duration when its message carries a duration_ms field. Entries without that field are left out without comment. When the value of the field is not a whole number written with digits only (for example 'n/a', '-3' or '12.5'), skip the entry and tell the user, with the timestamp and the source of the entry. At the end, tell the user how many durations were used and how many entries were skipped.

Group the durations by source. For each source, compute the count, the median, the 95th percentile and the maximum, all in milliseconds. The median and the 95th percentile are nearest-rank percentiles: for percentile p of n durations sorted from small to large, take the duration at position ceil(p * n / 100), counting from 1. For example, the median of 4 durations is the second smallest one.

Write OUTPUT_CSV with the header `source,count,median,p95,max` and one row per source that has at least one duration, sorted by source name. All values are whole numbers. When no entry has a usable duration, the file holds only the header. The command then exits with status 0.

If one of the FILE arguments does not exist, the command must exit with status 2 and must not create OUTPUT_CSV.

Add tests for the new feature.
